# Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 (Game Boy Advance video game)

## 1. Introduction

Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the Game Boy Advance (GBA) is a 2001 sports video game developed by Vicarious Visions and published by Activision . It is the handheld adaptation of the critically acclaimed console game Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2, which was originally developed by Neversoft . The GBA version was released on May 30, 2001, in North America, June 22, 2001, in Europe, and December 14, 2001, in Japan .

The game is notable for successfully translating the 3D skateboarding experience to the GBA's 2D hardware through an innovative isometric perspective . Players control professional skateboarders performing tricks and completing objectives across various levels, earning cash to purchase upgrades and new equipment .

## 2. Development and release

### 2.1 Development team

The Game Boy Advance version of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 was developed by Vicarious Visions, an American video game developer . This marked Vicarious Visions' first major project in the Tony Hawk series, as the console versions were developed by Neversoft . The game's development was led by Jason Uyeda as director, with Scott Pease serving as producer .

The development team faced significant technical challenges in porting the 3D console game to the GBA's 2D hardware. To overcome these limitations, they implemented an isometric perspective with prerendered 3D backgrounds and 300-polygon 3D character models . This technical approach allowed the game to maintain the core gameplay mechanics while adapting to the handheld's hardware constraints.

### 2.2 Release dates and regions

The game was released in three main regions with staggered release dates:

* North America: May 30, 2001 

* Europe: June 22, 2001 

* Japan: December 14, 2001 (released as "SK8: Tony Hawk no Pro Skater 2") 

In Japan, the game was published by Success rather than Activision, and received a slightly different title . The staggered release dates allowed the development team to refine the game based on early market feedback and regional preferences.

### 2.3 Technical specifications

The GBA version featured several technical innovations to bring the Tony Hawk experience to the handheld platform:

* **Graphics**: The game used an isometric perspective with prerendered 3D backgrounds and 300-polygon 3D character models

* **Performance**: The game ran at a smooth 60 frames per second

* **Sound**: The game utilized Shin'en's GAX sound engine, with music composed by Shin'en developers 

* **Controls**: The game used a modified control scheme adapted to the GBA's limited button layout: L for kickflips, R for grinds, B for jumping, and A for grab moves

## 3. Gameplay

### 3.1 Overview

Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the GBA retains the core gameplay mechanics from the console versions while adapting to the handheld platform's limitations . The game features a third-person perspective with a fixed camera, allowing players to control professional or fictional skaters through various skateboarding challenges .

The game's physics system maintains a "loose grip on physics for the sake of gameplay quality," allowing players to perform unrealistic but entertaining trick combinations . This design philosophy prioritizes fun and accessibility over realistic physics simulation.

### 3.2 Game modes

The game offers several distinct game modes:

**Career Mode** is the main single-player experience where players guide their chosen skater through various skate spots with a checklist of goals and competitions . Instead of collecting tapes as in the first game, skaters earn money that can be used to buy decks, upgrade stats, and purchase new tricks . Beating this mode unlocks additional skaters, cheats, and new levels.

**Single Session** mode allows players to play in a level for a high score with a two-minute time limit. After completing a session with a good enough score, players can enter their initials for the high score table .

**Free Skate** mode permits skaters to stay in levels with no time limit, allowing players to practice, find secrets, or explore missing gaps .

### 3.3 Skaters and customization

The game features 13 professional skateboarders and 3 secret characters /Characters). The professional skaters include:

* Tony Hawk

* Bob Burnquist

* Steve Caballero

* Kareem Campbell

* Rune Glifberg

* Eric Koston

* Bucky Lasek

* Rodney Mullen

* Chad Muska

* Andrew Reynolds

* Geoff Rowley

* Elissa Steamer

* Jamie Thomas

The three secret characters are Spider-Man (via a licensing agreement with Marvel Comics), Mindy (exclusive to the GBA version), and McSkib /Characters).

Each skater has unique attributes in ten categories: Air, Hangtime, Ollie, Speed, Spin, Landing, Switch, Rail Balance, Lip Balance, and Manuals . Players can customize their skater's appearance by choosing different skateboard graphics and adjusting truck settings to make the skateboard easier or harder to turn .

### 3.4 Tricks and scoring system

The game features an extensive trick system allowing players to perform various skateboarding maneuvers . While airborne, skaters can execute two types of moves:

**Flip tricks** are performed by pressing a direction with the A and B buttons simultaneously . **Grab tricks** are executed by pressing a direction with the A button only. Most grab tricks and some flip tricks can be held for additional points .

The scoring system rewards players for stringing together combos. Performing two or more tricks creates a combo multiplier that increases with each successful trick . The game also introduces "landing ratings" where the straightness of a landing affects the score - landing straight earns a "green perfect" rating with a 50% score increase, while landing diagonally results in a "red sloppy" rating with a 30% score reduction .

### 3.5 Levels and objectives

The game features seven levels in total: four regular levels, two competition levels, and one secret level . The levels include:

1. **Hangar - Meacham Field, Texas**

* Objectives: 10,000/25,000/75,000 points; collect SKATE letters; hit 5 barrels; find 5 pilot wings; 3 hangtime gaps; nosegrind over the pipe; secret tape

1. **School II - Southern California**

* Objectives: 15,000/40,000/100,000 points; collect SKATE letters; wallride 5 bells; find 5 hall passes; 3 Roll Call rails; kickflip TC's roof; secret tape

1. **Marseille - Marseille, France** (Competition level)

* First competition level, requires \$3,000 to access

1. **Warehouse - Troy, New York**

* Objectives: 20,000/50,000/150,000 points; collect SKATE letters; destroy 5 crates; find 5 spray cans; 3 Oldskool gaps; 5-0 the Big Rail; secret tape

1. **NY City - New York City, New York**

* Objectives: 50,000/125,000/250,000 points; collect SKATE letters; ollie 3 hydrants; find 5 subway tokens; 3 Blue Cow gaps; 50-50 TC's Sculpture; secret tape

1. **Skatestreet - Ventura, California** (Competition level)

* Second competition level, requires \$35,000 to access

1. **Rooftops - Boston, Massachusetts** (Secret level)

* Unlockable level, requires beating Career Mode 100% with all skaters (except Spider-Man and Mindy)

### 3.6 Special features

The GBA version includes several special features that differentiate it from other handheld versions:

**The Special Meter** fills up by landing tricks without bailing. When full, the skater enters special mode where attributes are enhanced and special moves can be performed . Special moves require complex inputs but reward significantly higher points.

**Gap system**: Gaps or transfers are spots in levels that reward points for skating off certain objects. They appear in the combo list in blue text and add to the multiplier .

**Kid Mode** can be toggled in options, making balancing and landing easier for younger players .

**Trick Zoom** zooms the camera in when performing special moves, providing a better view of the action .

## 4. Reception and reviews

### 4.1 Critical reception

Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the GBA received universal critical acclaim upon release . Review aggregator website Metacritic identified it as having received universal acclaim, labeling it a "must-play" . The game maintained an aggregate score of 98/100 on Metacritic, making it the second highest-rated game of all time at the time, behind only The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time .

Reviewers particularly praised the game's technical achievements. Nintendo World Report stated: "It's that simple. Not that the GBA needs any help, but Tony Hawk is an awesome game. Actually, it's one of the most flawless games in recent memory" . The publication noted that the game "translates the style and sense of the game accurately into an isometric (pseudo-3D or 2.5D) game" .

Kidzworld praised the game's graphics, stating: "The GBA isn't supposed to be able to do 3D graphics but that didn't stop the Hawk - he pulled off sweet 3D skater graphics. I don't think even Nintendo knows how to make games look this good" .

However, some reviewers noted minor criticisms. HonestGamers mentioned that the sound quality "isn't actually that great, often sounding somewhat 'tinny', especially when you hear it on headphones" . Some reviewers also noted that the isometric perspective took time to adjust to, with one reviewer stating: "The first time you play it's really catastrophic! The handling is delicate and it will take a fairly long time to adapt" .

### 4.2 Awards and nominations

The GBA version was nominated for "Outstanding Achievement in Handheld Game" at the 2002 Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences awards . However, it lost to Advance Wars.

### 4.3 Commercial performance

While specific sales figures for the GBA version are not available, the overall Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 franchise sold approximately 7.25 million copies across all platforms . The GBA version was part of Activision's strategy to maximize revenue by releasing the game on multiple platforms, including handhelds.

The game was commercially successful enough to warrant a place on multiple "best GBA games" lists. It was included in IGN's list of "25 best GBA games" and Cultured Vultures' "50 best GBA games of all time," with the latter noting: "Porting a game as vast and complex as Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 to the much simpler Game Boy Advance surprisingly worked out well for everyone concerned" .

## 5. Legacy and impact

### 5.1 Technical innovations

The GBA version of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 is remembered for its technical achievements in bringing 3D gameplay to a 2D handheld . The game was elected as the first handheld game in 3D and was the first in the series to feature create-a-skater options .

The game's use of prerendered 3D backgrounds combined with 3D character models running at 60 frames per second was considered groundbreaking for the GBA at the time . This technical approach influenced future GBA games that attempted to bring 3D experiences to the handheld platform.

### 5.2 Cultural impact

The Tony Hawk's Pro Skater series, including the GBA version, had a significant cultural impact on video games and popular culture . The games helped popularize extreme sports video games and introduced many players to the world of professional skateboarding.

The GBA version's success demonstrated the viability of porting console-quality games to handheld platforms, encouraging other developers to attempt similar ambitious ports. The game's inclusion of licensed music (though adapted for the GBA) and professional athletes also set a standard for sports games on handhelds.

### 5.3 Franchise evolution

The success of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 across all platforms, including the GBA, led to numerous sequels and spin-offs in the series . The GBA version specifically influenced how future Tony Hawk games would be designed for handheld platforms.

Later entries in the series would expand on features introduced in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2, including improved create-a-skater modes, more complex trick systems, and expanded career modes. The GBA version's successful adaptation of console gameplay to a handheld served as a template for future handheld sports games.

## 6. Conclusion

Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the Game Boy Advance stands as a remarkable achievement in handheld gaming history. Developed by Vicarious Visions and published by Activision, the game successfully brought the console skateboarding experience to the GBA through innovative technical solutions and thoughtful design decisions.

The game's critical success, with a 98/100 score on Metacritic and universal acclaim from reviewers, demonstrated that ambitious console ports to handhelds were not only possible but could achieve the same high standards as their console counterparts . The game's commercial success and cultural impact helped establish the Tony Hawk's Pro Skater series as a cornerstone of sports gaming.

The technical innovations employed in the GBA version, including the use of isometric perspective, 3D character models, and 60fps performance, pushed the boundaries of what was possible on the Game Boy Advance . These innovations influenced future handheld game development and demonstrated the potential of the platform for complex 3D experiences.

Today, Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the Game Boy Advance is remembered as one of the best handheld games of its era, maintaining a strong fan base and appearing on numerous "best of" lists . The game's legacy continues through modern re-releases and remasters of the Tony Hawk's Pro Skater series, ensuring that new generations of players can experience the game that helped define handheld sports gaming.

statements.fact: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the Game Boy Advance (GBA) is a 2001 sports video game developed by Vicarious Visions and published by Activision.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the Game Boy Advance (GBA) is the handheld adaptation of the critically acclaimed console game Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2, which was originally developed by Neversoft.
The GBA version of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 was released on May 30, 2001, in North America.
The GBA version of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 was released on June 22, 2001, in Europe.
The GBA version of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 was released on December 14, 2001, in Japan.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the GBA is notable for successfully translating the 3D skateboarding experience to the GBA's 2D hardware through an innovative isometric perspective.
Players in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the GBA control professional skateboarders performing tricks and completing objectives across various levels.
Players in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the GBA earn cash to purchase upgrades and new equipment.
The Game Boy Advance version of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 was developed by Vicarious Visions, an American video game developer.
This marked Vicarious Visions' first major project in the Tony Hawk series.
The console versions of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 were developed by Neversoft.
The development of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA was led by Jason Uyeda as director.
Scott Pease served as producer for Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA.
The development team for Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA faced significant technical challenges in porting the 3D console game to the GBA's 2D hardware.
To overcome limitations, the development team for Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA implemented an isometric perspective with prerendered 3D backgrounds and 300-polygon 3D character models.
This technical approach allowed Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA to maintain the core gameplay mechanics while adapting to the handheld's hardware constraints.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA was released in North America on May 30, 2001.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA was released in Europe on June 22, 2001.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA was released in Japan on December 14, 2001.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA was released in Japan as "SK8: Tony Hawk no Pro Skater 2".
In Japan, Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA was published by Success rather than Activision.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA received a slightly different title in Japan.
The staggered release dates for Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA allowed the development team to refine the game based on early market feedback and regional preferences.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA used an isometric perspective with prerendered 3D backgrounds and 300-polygon 3D character models for its graphics.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA ran at a smooth 60 frames per second.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA utilized Shin'en's GAX sound engine.
Music for Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA was composed by Shin'en developers.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA used a modified control scheme adapted to the GBA's limited button layout.
In Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA, L is used for kickflips.
In Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA, R is used for grinds.
In Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA, B is used for jumping.
In Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA, A is used for grab moves.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the GBA retains the core gameplay mechanics from the console versions.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the GBA adapts to the handheld platform's limitations.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the GBA features a third-person perspective with a fixed camera.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the GBA allows players to control professional or fictional skaters through various skateboarding challenges.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the GBA's physics system maintains a "loose grip on physics for the sake of gameplay quality".
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the GBA allows players to perform unrealistic but entertaining trick combinations.
The design philosophy of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the GBA prioritizes fun and accessibility over realistic physics simulation.
Career Mode in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA is the main single-player experience.
In Career Mode, players guide their chosen skater through various skate spots with a checklist of goals and competitions.
In Career Mode of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA, skaters earn money that can be used to buy decks, upgrade stats, and purchase new tricks, instead of collecting tapes as in the first game.
Beating Career Mode in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA unlocks additional skaters, cheats, and new levels.
Single Session mode in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA allows players to play in a level for a high score with a two-minute time limit.
After completing a session with a good enough score in Single Session mode, players can enter their initials for the high score table.
Free Skate mode in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA permits skaters to stay in levels with no time limit.
Free Skate mode allows players to practice, find secrets, or explore missing gaps.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA features 13 professional skateboarders.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA features 3 secret characters.

The professional skaters in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA include Tony Hawk, Bob Burnquist, Steve Caballero, Kareem Campbell, Rune Glifberg, Eric Koston, Bucky Lasek, Rodney Mullen, Chad Muska, Andrew Reynolds, Geoff Rowley, Elissa Steamer, and Jamie Thomas.
The three secret characters in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA are Spider-Man, Mindy, and McSkib.
Spider-Man is a secret character in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA via a licensing agreement with Marvel Comics.
Mindy is a secret character exclusive to the GBA version of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2.
Each skater in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA has unique attributes in ten categories: Air, Hangtime, Ollie, Speed, Spin, Landing, Switch, Rail Balance, Lip Balance, and Manuals.
Players can customize their skater's appearance in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA by choosing different skateboard graphics.
Players can customize their skater's appearance in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA by adjusting truck settings to make the skateboard easier or harder to turn.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA features an extensive trick system allowing players to perform various skateboarding maneuvers.
Flip tricks in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA are performed by pressing a direction with the A and B buttons simultaneously.
Grab tricks in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA are executed by pressing a direction with the A button only.
Most grab tricks and some flip tricks in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA can be held for additional points.
The scoring system in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA rewards players for stringing together combos.
Performing two or more tricks in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA creates a combo multiplier that increases with each successful trick.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA introduces "landing ratings" where the straightness of a landing affects the score.
Landing straight in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA earns a "green perfect" rating with a 50% score increase.
Landing diagonally in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA results in a "red sloppy" rating with a 30% score reduction.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA features seven levels in total: four regular levels, two competition levels, and one secret level.

The Hangar - Meacham Field, Texas level in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA has objectives including 10,000/25,000/75,000 points, collecting SKATE letters, hitting 5 barrels, finding 5 pilot wings, 3 hangtime gaps, nosegrinding over the pipe, and finding a secret tape.

The School II - Southern California level in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA has objectives including 15,000/40,000/100,000 points, collecting SKATE letters, wallriding 5 bells, finding 5 hall passes, 3 Roll Call rails, kickflipping TC's roof, and finding a secret tape.
Marseille - Marseille, France is a competition level in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA.
The Marseille - Marseille, France competition level requires $3,000 to access.

The Warehouse - Troy, New York level in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA has objectives including 20,000/50,000/150,000 points, collecting SKATE letters, destroying 5 crates, finding 5 spray cans, 3 Oldskool gaps, 5-0ing the Big Rail, and finding a secret tape.

The NY City - New York City, New York level in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA has objectives including 50,000/125,000/250,000 points, collecting SKATE letters, ollieing 3 hydrants, finding 5 subway tokens, 3 Blue Cow gaps, 50-50ing TC's Sculpture, and finding a secret tape.
Skatestreet - Ventura, California is a competition level in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA.
The Skatestreet - Ventura, California competition level requires $35,000 to access.
Rooftops - Boston, Massachusetts is a secret level in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA.
The Rooftops - Boston, Massachusetts secret level is unlockable.
The Rooftops - Boston, Massachusetts secret level requires beating Career Mode 100% with all skaters (except Spider-Man and Mindy) to unlock.
The Special Meter in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA fills up by landing tricks without bailing.
When the Special Meter is full, the skater enters special mode where attributes are enhanced and special moves can be performed.
Special moves in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA require complex inputs but reward significantly higher points.
Gaps or transfers are spots in levels that reward points for skating off certain objects.
Gaps appear in the combo list in blue text and add to the multiplier.
Kid Mode can be toggled in options in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA.
Kid Mode makes balancing and landing easier for younger players.
Trick Zoom in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA zooms the camera in when performing special moves.
Trick Zoom provides a better view of the action.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the GBA received universal critical acclaim upon release.
Review aggregator website Metacritic identified Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA as having received universal acclaim.
Metacritic labeled Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA a "must-play".
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA maintained an aggregate score of 98/100 on Metacritic.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA was the second highest-rated game of all time at the time, behind only The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
Reviewers particularly praised the game's technical achievements.
Nintendo World Report stated: "It's that simple. Not that the GBA needs any help, but Tony Hawk is an awesome game. Actually, it's one of the most flawless games in recent memory".
Nintendo World Report noted that Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA "translates the style and sense of the game accurately into an isometric (pseudo-3D or 2.5D) game".
Kidzworld praised the graphics of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA.

Kidzworld stated about Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA: "The GBA isn't supposed to be able to do 3D graphics but that didn't stop the Hawk - he pulled off sweet 3D skater graphics. I don't think even Nintendo knows how to make games look this good".
HonestGamers mentioned that the sound quality of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA "isn't actually that great, often sounding somewhat 'tinny', especially when you hear it on headphones".
Some reviewers noted that the isometric perspective of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA took time to adjust to.
One reviewer stated about Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA: "The first time you play it's really catastrophic! The handling is delicate and it will take a fairly long time to adapt".
The GBA version of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 was nominated for "Outstanding Achievement in Handheld Game" at the 2002 Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences awards.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA lost to Advance Wars at the 2002 Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences awards.
The overall Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 franchise sold approximately 7.25 million copies across all platforms.
The GBA version of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 was part of Activision's strategy to maximize revenue by releasing the game on multiple platforms, including handhelds.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA was commercially successful enough to warrant a place on multiple "best GBA games" lists.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA was included in IGN's list of "25 best GBA games".
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA was included in Cultured Vultures' "50 best GBA games of all time".

Cultured Vultures noted about Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA: "Porting a game as vast and complex as Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 to the much simpler Game Boy Advance surprisingly worked out well for everyone concerned".
The GBA version of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 is remembered for its technical achievements in bringing 3D gameplay to a 2D handheld.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA was elected as the first handheld game in 3D.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA was the first in the series to feature create-a-skater options.
The game's use of prerendered 3D backgrounds combined with 3D character models running at 60 frames per second was considered groundbreaking for the GBA at the time.
This technical approach influenced future GBA games that attempted to bring 3D experiences to the handheld platform.
The Tony Hawk's Pro Skater series, including the GBA version, had a significant cultural impact on video games and popular culture.
The Tony Hawk's Pro Skater games helped popularize extreme sports video games.
The Tony Hawk's Pro Skater games introduced many players to the world of professional skateboarding.
The GBA version's success demonstrated the viability of porting console-quality games to handheld platforms.
The GBA version's success encouraged other developers to attempt similar ambitious ports.
The GBA version's inclusion of licensed music (though adapted for the GBA) set a standard for sports games on handhelds.
The GBA version's inclusion of professional athletes set a standard for sports games on handhelds.
The success of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 across all platforms, including the GBA, led to numerous sequels and spin-offs in the series.
The GBA version specifically influenced how future Tony Hawk games would be designed for handheld platforms.

Later entries in the Tony Hawk's Pro Skater series would expand on features introduced in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2, including improved create-a-skater modes, more complex trick systems, and expanded career modes.
The GBA version's successful adaptation of console gameplay to a handheld served as a template for future handheld sports games.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the Game Boy Advance stands as a remarkable achievement in handheld gaming history.

Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for GBA successfully brought the console skateboarding experience to the GBA through innovative technical solutions and thoughtful design decisions.

The game's commercial success helped establish the Tony Hawk's Pro Skater series as a cornerstone of sports gaming.
The game's cultural impact helped establish the Tony Hawk's Pro Skater series as a cornerstone of sports gaming.

These innovations influenced future handheld game development.
These innovations demonstrated the potential of the platform for complex 3D experiences.
Today, Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the Game Boy Advance is remembered as one of the best handheld games of its era.
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 for the Game Boy Advance maintains a strong fan base.

Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 :: GBA Game Review
===========================================

Dec 27, 2006

All hail Tony Hawk! It's time to quit all those other religions and bow down to the one true God (kidding!) Ok, so he's not that good but man, is he close. The latest version of [**Tony Hawk's Pro Skater (THPS)**](https://www.kidzworld.com/article/154-tony-hawks-pro-skater-2-for-playstation "Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 :: Playstation Game Review") may come in a small package but it's a [**big game**](https://www.kidzworld.com/article/3381-the-lost-vikings-gba "The Lost Vikings GBA"). All the skating, grinding, trick pulling action of the world's greatest skater has been packed into a teensy Game Boy Advance (GBA) cartridge. It lacks nothing. Now you can score points, hit combos and grind like mad wherever you want.

Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 Has the Moves
--------------------------------------

 The GBA isn't supposed to be able to do 3D graphics but that didn't stop the Hawk - he pulled off sweet 3D skater graphics. I don't think even [Nintendo](http://www.nintendo.com/) knows how to make games look this good. [**Tony Hawk's Pro Skater**](https://www.kidzworld.com/article/3493-gamecube-tony-hawks-pro-skater-3 "Gamecube - Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3") veterans will notice that they can't rotate the screen but that's the only problem with the graphics.

Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 Wipeout!
---------------------------------

The biggest bummer is the sound effects. All the regular grinds, bumps, thumps and groans are perfect but there's no way to pack a CD worth of [cool tunes](https://www.kidzworld.com/site/Tunes.htm) onto a cartridge the size of your thumb. The Hawk's big-name skater bands can't come out and party so you'll have to make do with boring beats and riffs.

Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 Final Grind
------------------------------------

Once you've fired up the game it's classic **THPS** action all the way. It plays just like the Playstation 2, [Dreamcast](https://www.kidzworld.com/article/946-it-lives "It Lives! The Sega Dreamcast") and Playstation versions. There are six levels, 13 skaters and hordes of tricks, bonuses and secrets to uncover. Once you've mastered some serious moves you'll be all set to conquer the levels, unlock secrets and kick butt.

How Hard is Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2?
-------------------------------------

 It'll take an hour to learn the controls and the game is hardcore.

------------------------------------

-----------------------------------

*    Tons of moves.
*    The Warehouse.
*    Skateboarding action for the gamer on the go.

Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 Thumbs Down:
-------------------------------------

*    No multiplayer.
*    No big-name tunes.

8.title: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 (Game Boy Advance) review
8.description: Coverage related to Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 (Game Boy Advance), provided by site staff and readers.
8.content:
**Introduction:**

I'm sure you've heard of the hit Tony Hawk games for Playstation, which 

 allowed gamers and skateboarding fans to play as their pro-idols like 

 Tony Hawk and Steve Caballero. I don't know a single person who doesn't 

 like the Tony Hawk games for Playstation, and I know very few who 

 dislike the GBA version. Packed into the tiny cartridge is a game almost as 

 entertaining and realistic as the console versions. Here you'll find 

 some of the same levels, all the same skaters, more moves, and a similar 

 layout and control. Any fans of the other Tony Hawk games are sure to 

 love this.

**Graphics:**

Probably the biggest standout in THPS2 are the graphics. All the 

 skaters are very simple polygons, but polygons none-the-less. This enables 

 them to move much more smoothly and realistically than sprites. While 

 the low-polygon characters have little detail, they get the job done on 

 the small screen, offering good animation and framerate. The 

 backgrounds are nice, 2D-rendered backdrops, with a very impressive amount of 

 detail, similar to something you'd find on the Playstation.

While the graphics are excellent for a handheld system, they're still 

 not quite everything everyone made them out to be. I heard things like 

 ''best graphics out of any GBA launch game'', and ''Just like the 

 playstation version.'' This is not the case. Even though they are very good, 

 there are some rather obvious problems. The biggest and probably the 

 most annoying problem is the high level of pixelation you'll find. 

 Because the polygon count is low, the characters look very pixelated, and 

 sometimes just look like a blob of little dots, unless you use your 

 imagination. Another one is the transparency issue. because the game is 

 from a 3/4 view, and not a top-down view, there are places where your 

 skater would get lost behind objects. To prevent this, the game 

 developers made transparencies, so that you could see your character, even when 

 he was behind something. While it's a good idea, the transparency is 

 often very confusing, and somewhat blurry and pixelated.

Overall, the graphics are very good, but to be a nit-picker, I named 

 the problems, just so people wouldn't set their sights too high.

**Sound:**

The sound is fairly good, with cool clicking sounds everytime you jump, 

 and music samples from the THPS2 on the Playstation. The only problem is 

 that the quality isn't actually that great, often sounding somewhat 

 ''tinny'', especially when you hear it on headphones. Aside from that, 

 there's no problem with the sound, and it creates a somewhat nice skating 

 atmosphere.

**Gameplay:**

Here is where the game really shows what a console port is all about. 

 Even though the game is from a fixed camera angle, those who have 

 played the Tony Hawk games for the Playstation will feel ''right at home'' because 

 the game mechanics and idea of the game are nearly identical. You 

 basically pick between three options: career mode, free skate, and single 

 session. The second too are fairly self explanatory, while the first is 

 a mode where you play through levels, trying to achieve certain goals, 

 and then proceeding onto more levels. In the end, the gameplay is 

 involving yet simple.

**Control:**

When I first started playing, I had a really rough time controlling my 

 skater. He wouldn't go where I wanted him to go, and I just couldn't 

 get the hang of it. 10 minutes later, I felt like an expert (even 

 though I wasn't.) The controls are hard at first, but easy to grasp after a 

 short practice session. They're very similar to those of the 

 Playstation games. B is jump, A is grind, and either of the L buttons execute 

 grabs. After you get the idea, you'll see that the control is actually 

 very tight, and controlling a miniature skateboarder on your screen has 

 never been easier.

**Conclusion:**

As a game which excels in pretty much all categories, you simply can't 

 go wrong. When I heard about this, I thought that it would be a 

 disaster, because I knew that the GBA hardware couldn't handle it. I was 

 proven wrong as soon as I started playing it, because somehow, Activision 

 pulled it off. And I thank them greatly for that, because now I have a 

 great portable skating game, almost as good as the Playstation game of 

 the same name.

**Breakdown:**

_Graphics:_ 9.5/10

_Sound:_ 8.5/10

_Gameplay:_ 9/10

_Control:_ 8.5/10

_Replay:_ 7.5/10

### Techniquement…

Là y’a pas à dire on prends vraiment **une grosse claque**

 ! C’est tout bonnement incroyable ! Les personnages sont criants de

 réalisme et les décors très détaillés, le tout est vraiment **très beau** ! Le GameBoy Advance en a dans le ventre, et Vicarious Visions nous le prouve ici majestueusement !

Par contre niveau jouabilité ça se gâte… On se doutait que le passage

 à une vue isométrique poserait quelques problèmes, mais la première

 fois qu’on y joue c’est réellement catastrophique ! **La prise en main est délicate**

 et il faudra un assez long temps d’adaptation (comptez une petite heure

 pour les plus forts d’entre vous et deux bonnes heures pour les gros

 débutants). Mais une fois qu’on est habitué, alors c’est un vrai

 bonheur !!! On enchaîne des figures incroyables et on explose

 littéralement tous les scores en un temps record ! Et des figures il y

 en a ! Chaque personnage possède des figures qui lui sont propres, et

 il est possible d’en racheter encore de nouvelles dans le mode

 carrière…

Quant aux musiques **elles sont bien rythmées et collent parfaitement à l’ambiance de folie**

 du jeu ! Ce ne sont plus les mêmes chansons que les versions salons

 mais simplement des versions “instrumentales”. Très variées et assez

 nombreuses elles ne sont pas prêtes de vous saouler (d’ailleurs si vous

 voulez un petit aperçu toutes les musiques du jeu sont disponibles dans

 sa section download).#row_end

### Les modes de jeu

Le jeu ne propose que 3 modes :

– **Simple session**

 : vous pourrez rider dans tous les niveaux débloqués en mode carrière

 dans des runs de 2 minutes, ce mode est assez utile pour essayer

 d’améliorer ses scores.

– **Skate libre** : là encore vous

 pourrez parcourir tous les niveaux déjà débloqués, mais cette fois-ci

 vous n’avez aucune limite de temps, ce qui s’avère assez pratique pour

 essayer de découvrir tous les gaps du jeu.

– **Mode Carrière**

 : c’est certainement le mode le plus intéressant du jeu. En effet vous

 devrez choisir un des 13 skaters et devrez le faire évoluer dans les 6

 niveaux du jeu. Dans chaque niveau vous devrez accomplir certaines

 missions (10 pour chaque niveau où vous devrez par exemple collecter

 les lettres S-K-A-T-E, faire un certains nombre de points, trouver une

 cassette secrète, etc…). Chaque mission effectuée vous rapporte une

 certaine somme d’argent que vous pourrez alors dépenser en augmentant

 les stats de votre skater, en achetant de nouvelles figures ou bien de

 nouveaux skates. Parmi les 6 niveaux on trouve deux compétitions où

 vous devrez cette fois-ci faire un maximum de points et remporter une

 médaille d’or. Bref ce mode est palpitant et c’est grâce à lui que vous

 pourrez débloquer un nouveau niveau (Les Toits à Boston) ou de nouveaux

 Cheats.

 Bref vous aurez largement de quoi faire et **la durée de vie est donc plus que bonne** (comptez entre 20 et 30 heures de jeu pour tout découvrir et tout débloquer sans tricher !).

### Conclusion

Graphiquement irréprochable et à la durée de vie

 excellente, Tony Hawks Pro Skater 2 comblera tous les fans de la série

 ou des jeux de sports de glisses en général. Quant aux autres Tony Hawk

 2 reste un excellent jeu, qui pourra toutefois leur paraître un peu

 lassant à force…

Information Die [Xbox](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox "Xbox")-Version erschien als _Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 2x._

**Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 2** ist der zweite Teil der [Skateboarding](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skateboarding "Skateboarding")-Videospielreihe _[Tony Hawk’s](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony\_Hawk%E2%80%99s "Tony Hawk’s")_ von [Activision](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activision "Activision"). Es wurde von [Neversoft](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neversoft "Neversoft") entwickelt und kam am 19. September 2000 zunächst für die [PlayStation](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation "PlayStation") auf den Markt. Am 6. November folgte eine Fassung für [Game Boy Color](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy_Color "Game Boy Color"). Eine Version für [Dreamcast](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamcast "Dreamcast") erschien am 7. November 2000. Die Portierung auf den PC wurde am 20. November 2000 veröffentlicht. Am 31. Mai 2001 erschien eine Fassung für [Game Boy Advance](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy_Advance "Game Boy Advance"). Für den [Nintendo 64](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_64 "Nintendo 64") erschien am 22. September 2001 eine Version. Zudem wurde das Spiel für den [Macintosh](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macintosh "Macintosh") herausgegeben. 2010 erschien eine Fassung für [iPhone](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone "IPhone").

Eine Neufassung von Entwickler [Treyarch](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treyarch "Treyarch") erschien mit _Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 2x_ am 12. November 2001 als [Launchtitel](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Launchtitel "Launchtitel") für die [Xbox](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox "Xbox"). Ein [Remaster](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computerspiel-Remaster "Computerspiel-Remaster") von _[Pro Skater](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony\_Hawk%E2%80%99s\_Pro\_Skater "Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater")_ und _Pro Skater 2_ erschien 2020 als _[Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 1 + 2](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony\_Hawk%E2%80%99s\_Pro\_Skater\_1\_%2B\_2 "Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 1 + 2")._

Wie im ersten Teil muss der Spieler Trick-Kombos in verschiedenen [Skateparks](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skatepark "Skatepark") alleine oder zu zweit vorführen. Die [Grafik](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computergrafik "Computergrafik") wurde verbessert und neue Parks eingeführt. Es gibt zahlreiche Tricks und Geheimlevels. Außerdem kann ein eigener Skatepark erstellt sowie die Skater mit verschiedener Kleidung ausgestattet werden.
